newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican Airways accuse BA partner of spying.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican Airways accuse BA partner of spying.

text.p: South African Airways (SAA) SAA.CN has accused domestic rival Comair, whose new franchise agreement with British Airways Plc took force on Sunday, of illegal spying into its computer database.
SAA claimed a Comair employee had tapped into its reservations computer and illegally extracted passenger information which could be used for commercial gain.
But privately-owned Comair said the timing of the allegations, splashed over the front page of the national Sunday Times newspaper, was suspicious.

"It seems very strange that the day our British Airways-Comair franchise came into operation was the day this was released, and we know they are very concerned about our operation at this stage," a spokesman told local radio.
The newspaper said Comair had denied the charges, but the airline could not immediately be reached for further comment.
SAA spokesman Leon Els confirmed that SAA's concerns had been passed on in a letter to Comair, the country's Business Practices Committee, and the police.
"We are waiting the outcome of their investigations," he told Reuters on Sunday.
In the letter, which was published in the Sunday Times, SAA chief executive Mike Myburgh said: "We believe this to be a criminal offence.
"Aspects of this appear similar to reported incidents of the 'dirty tricks' campaign used by BA against Virgin Airlines on the North Atlantic (route)."
BA had to pay damages for saying Virgin had lied when it accused BA of taking information from its computer to try to target passengers and lure them away.
Virgin has also teamed up with local partner, Sun Air, as competition hots up in the South African skies.
Local radio quoted "industry insiders" as saying that much of the information Comair gleaned was freely available to travel agents, and that Comair had paid to access it.
But Els said this was inaccurate and that Comair had obtained much more detailed information on passengers.
